title: OK Corral

source.quote: Though we switch between quadrants on the Corral, we each have one 'favorite' quadrant where we spend most of our time while in script.

setting: Monday, 9:05am. The warehouse floor is already loud. Diego has run this shift for two years and prides himself on never letting anything slip.

L1.line: Don't bring me small stuff. Figure it out yourself - that's literally your job.
cues: doesn't look up from his clipboard
already walking off before she can answer
L1.question: Quick primer: the OK Corral is a simple map of four stances we take toward ourselves and the other person in a moment - I'm-OK/You're-OK, I'm-not-OK/You're-OK, I'm-OK/You're-not-OK, and I'm-not-OK/You're-not-OK - each one paired with a go-to move: Get-On-With, Get-Away-From, Get-Rid-Of, or Get-Nowhere-With. Priti just asked Diego a quick clarifying question about the delivery schedule. Which OK Corral position is Diego speaking from?

options.text: I'm OK, you're OK - he's being efficient, delegating clearly.
options.feedback: Get-On-With from Adult can sound brief, sure - but it stays curious and leaves the door open for a real answer. This closes the door before she's said a word.

options.text: I'm not-OK, you're OK - he feels overwhelmed and is deferring to her judgment.
options.feedback: Deferring upward is the next quadrant's move. Nothing here suggests Diego sees Priti as more capable than him - he's dismissing her, not deferring to her.

options.text: I'm OK, you're not-OK - he's getting rid of a problem he's decided isn't worth his attention.
options.feedback: Right. This is Get-Rid-Of done from Child, not Adult: the content could pass for healthy delegation, but the sharp tone and the refusal to even hear the question out is one-up, not fair.

options.text: I'm not-OK, you're not-OK - he's given up on the whole situation.
options.feedback: Get-Nowhere-With sounds defeated or resigned. Diego isn't resigned here - he's dismissive and clearly still in charge. That's the one-up quadrant, not the futility one.

L1.lesson: Get-Rid-Of can be done from Adult (clear, fair, leaves both people OK) or from Child (one-up, dismissive, quietly 'confirming' I'm-OK-you're-not). The content of a line doesn't tell you which - the tone and the follow-through do.

L2.intro: Track Diego's OK Corral position across one ordinary shift. Same four positions each time; the operation he reaches for is the tell.

beats.line: Diego - I sent the wrong pallet out on the 8am run. The client already called. I'm sorry.
cues: holding the manifest against her chest like a shield

options.text: This is exactly why I check everything myself. Go. I'll fix it.
options.outcome: Priti shrinks and backs off. The pallet gets sorted within the hour - but she stops mentioning small mistakes to him early, from now on.
options.lesson: Get-Rid-Of from Child looks capable in the moment, but 'I'll fix it myself' trains people to hide problems from you instead of bringing them early - a short-term win that 'confirms' I'm-OK-you're-not at a real cost.

options.text: Oh no - I probably should've double-checked the manifest myself. This one's on me too.
options.outcome: Priti looks relieved, but confused - it wasn't his mistake. Diego absorbs blame that was never his to carry.
options.lesson: Get-Away-From by way of self-blame reflects I'm-not-OK-you're-OK. It's generous, and it protects the relationship, but it reinforces a not-OK view of himself that wasn't actually called for here.

options.text: Walk me through what happened, then let's call the client together.
options.outcome: They map the error in ninety seconds and call the client together. The client calms down fast, hearing an actual plan instead of an apology alone.
options.lesson: Get-On-With chosen in Adult, not stumbled into. Ernst calls I'm-OK-you're-OK the only position based on reality - which is exactly why it looks unremarkable next to the other three.

options.text: Ugh. Nothing goes right on this shift, does it.
options.outcome: Priti doesn't know what to say to that. The mistake still needs fixing, and now the mood on the floor has dropped with it.
options.lesson: Get-Nowhere-With doesn't make the problem smaller - it just adds futility on top of it. If this becomes Diego's habit, it's the payoff a banal script is quietly aiming for.

beats.line: I heard about this morning's mix-up, Diego. In front of everyone: 'Can we get some basic quality control around here?'
cues: said loudly enough for the whole floor to hear
doesn't ask what actually happened before saying it

options.text: (Say nothing. Stare at the floor. Feel the old 'I never get it right' settle in.)
options.outcome: The team notices him go quiet. Fatima moves on to the next item. Diego carries the sting all afternoon, and snaps at Priti again later for something small.
options.lesson: This is the position we fall back to under stress, not the one we live in most of the day - Ernst's Corralogram can show a completely different quadrant in the same twenty-four hours.

options.text: That's not accurate. Here's what happened and how it's already resolved.
options.outcome: Fatima pauses, visibly recalibrating. She mutters a half-acknowledgment and moves on. The team sees Diego hold his ground without steamrolling anyone.
options.lesson: Get-On-With doesn't mean staying silent or agreeing - it means staying in Adult while still stating the facts plainly, even toward someone above you.

options.text: Must be nice to swoop in and judge after the fact.
options.outcome: Satisfying for about three seconds. Fatima bristles, and now there's a second small conflict stacked on top of the first one.
options.lesson: Get-Rid-Of toward Fatima discharges the sting but creates a new problem - the impulse to push back was fair; doing it from Child instead of Adult is what makes it costly.

options.text: Yeah, well, nothing I do is ever right around here anyway.
options.outcome: Awkward silence. Nobody on the team quite knows where to look.
options.lesson: Get-Nowhere-With doesn't protect Diego from the criticism - it just adds a line to the record that nothing here ever goes right, which is the belief the whole pattern exists to confirm.

fields.label: Sketch your own Corralogram for an ordinary day this week: which OK Corral quadrant gets the most square inches, and what's one Adult operation you could try there instead of the scripty version?

echo.setting: 48 hours later, Saturday morning, Diego's own kitchen.
echo.line: His son knocks over the orange juice reaching for the cereal. Diego's first words are already halfway out: 'Can you not? Just - go, I'll clean it.'
